questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: 1 newton is the force that accelerates 1 kg at 1 m/s².

questions.prompt: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Red is about 620–750 nm; violet is the shortest, at about 380–450 nm.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: From the Latin "aurum". Ag is silver, from "argentum".

questions.prompt: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: About 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

questions.prompt: Diamond and graphite are made of the same element.
questions.explanation: Both are pure carbon (allotropes). Only the way the atoms bond is different.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is called the "powerhouse of the cell"?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria make most of the cell's ATP through cellular respiration.

questions.prompt: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: Two atria and two ventricles.

questions.prompt: What is the derivative of x² with respect to x?
questions.explanation: Power rule: d/dx (xⁿ) = n·xⁿ⁻¹.

questions.prompt: Gravity on the Moon is roughly what fraction of gravity on Earth?
questions.explanation: About 1.6 m/s² on the Moon vs 9.8 m/s² on Earth.

questions.prompt: If you drop a hammer and a feather together in a vacuum, they hit the ground at the same time.
questions.explanation: Astronaut David Scott showed this on the Moon during Apollo 15 in 1971. No air means no air resistance.

questions.prompt: Which element is the most electronegative?
questions.explanation: Fluorine tops the Pauling scale at 3.98.

questions.prompt: Which compound is known as "laughing gas"?
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide (N₂O), used as a mild anaesthetic.

questions.prompt: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin covers about 2 m² in an adult. The liver is the largest internal organ.

questions.prompt: Mature human red blood cells have a nucleus.
questions.explanation: They lose their nucleus as they mature, which leaves more room for haemoglobin.

questions.prompt: What is 0! (zero factorial)?
questions.explanation: There is exactly one way to arrange nothing, and 0! = 1 keeps n! = n × (n−1)! working for n = 1.

questions.prompt: What is log₂ 1024?
What is the escape velocity from Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: 7.9 km/s is only enough to orbit Earth; 11.2 km/s gets you away for good.

questions.prompt: What is the hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethyne (C₂H₂)?
questions.explanation: The triple bond leaves each carbon with two electron domains, so it is sp and the molecule is linear.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme unzips the DNA double helix during replication?
questions.explanation: Helicase breaks the hydrogen bonds between base pairs; DNA polymerase then builds the new strands.

questions.prompt: Complete Euler's identity:  e^(iπ) + 1 = ?
questions.explanation: Often called the most beautiful equation in maths: it links e, i, π, 1 and 0.

questions.prompt: What does NIET stand for?
options: Nepal Institute of Engineering and Technology
National Institute of Engineering and Technology
National Institute of Education and Technology
National Institute of Electronics and Technology
questions.explanation: National Institute of Engineering and Technology. Say it three times fast!

questions.prompt: Who is the Principal of NIET?
questions.explanation: Now you know who to thank for this orientation!

questions.prompt: In which year was NIET established?
questions.explanation: It's right there on the seal: ESTD 2005.

questions.prompt: NIET is affiliated with which university?
questions.explanation: All BE and BTech programs at NIET are affiliated with Purbanchal University.

questions.prompt: NIET's newest program is the BTech in Artificial Intelligence.
questions.explanation: It joins BE Biomedical and BE Computer Engineering as the third program.

questions.prompt: Which river flows just north of the NIET campus?
questions.explanation: Kupondole sits on the south bank of the Bagmati. Cross the Thapathali bridge and you're in Kathmandu.

questions.prompt: Which three words appear on the NIET seal?
questions.explanation: Happy · Healthy · Learning. (Innovate · Lead · Transform are NIET's values, a sneaky trap!)

questions.prompt: NIET began as Nepal's first college for which engineering discipline?
questions.explanation: NIET pioneered Biomedical Engineering education in Nepal.

questions.prompt: Complete NIET's tagline: "Where innovation begins and …"
questions.explanation: "Where innovation begins and evolves."

questions.prompt: When it started in 2005, what was NIET called?
options: College of Biomedical Engineering and Applied Sciences
questions.explanation: CBEAS: the College of Biomedical Engineering and Applied Sciences.

questions.prompt: NIET was the first engineering college in Kathmandu Valley to receive QAA accreditation from which body?
questions.explanation: UGC Nepal awarded NIET its QAA Institutional Accreditation.

questions.prompt: In which year did Nepal's Ministry of Education name NIET the Best Private Engineering College?
What has keys but can't open any locks?
questions.explanation: You probably touched one today already.

questions.prompt: How many months of the year have 28 days?
questions.explanation: Every month has at least 28 days. February just stops there.

questions.prompt: What gets wetter the more it dries?
questions.explanation: It dries you, and gets wetter doing it.

questions.prompt: You are running a race and overtake the person in 2nd place. What place are you in now?
questions.explanation: You took their spot, so you're 2nd. First place is still ahead of you!

questions.prompt: What has hands but can't clap?
questions.explanation: Two hands, zero applause.

questions.prompt: Bananas are berries, but strawberries are not.
questions.explanation: Botanically, a banana is a berry. A strawberry's "seeds" sit on the outside, so it doesn't qualify.

questions.prompt: A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 9 run away. How many are left?
questions.explanation: "All but 9" means 9 stayed behind.

questions.prompt: Which is heavier: 1 kg of iron or 1 kg of cotton?
questions.explanation: A kilogram is a kilogram!

questions.prompt: What can you catch but can't throw?
questions.explanation: Or a bus, if you run fast enough.

questions.prompt: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
questions.explanation: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once, but only about 225 to orbit the Sun.

questions.prompt: How many times can you subtract 5 from 25?
questions.explanation: After the first time, you're subtracting from 20!

questions.prompt: Mary's father has five daughters: Nana, Nene, Nini and Nono. What is the fifth daughter's name?
questions.explanation: The answer was in the question all along.

questions.prompt: Before Mount Everest was discovered, what was the highest mountain in the world?
questions.explanation: It was still the highest. Nobody had measured it yet!

questions.prompt: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
questions.explanation: One M in "minute", two in "moment", and none in "a thousand years".

questions.prompt: A bat and a ball cost Rs 110 in total. The bat costs Rs 100 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?
questions.explanation: Ball Rs 5, bat Rs 105: the difference is Rs 100 and the total is Rs 110. (Rs 10 is the trap!)

questions.prompt: Which word is spelled incorrectly in every dictionary?
questions.explanation: Every dictionary spells it i-n-c-o-r-r-e-c-t-l-y. 😄

questions.prompt: Engineers once found a real moth trapped inside a computer and taped it into their logbook as a "bug".
questions.explanation: In 1947, the Harvard Mark II team logged it as the "first actual case of bug being found".

questions.prompt: What does CPU stand for?
questions.explanation: The CPU is the computer's brain: it carries out the instructions of a program.

questions.prompt: Which company created ChatGPT?
questions.explanation: OpenAI released ChatGPT in November 2022.

questions.prompt: An ECG records the electrical activity of which organ?
questions.explanation: ECG = electrocardiogram. For the brain, it would be an EEG.

questions.prompt: What is the binary number 1010 in decimal?
Which programming language is named after a comedy group, not a snake?
questions.explanation: Guido van Rossum named it after the British comedy show Monty Python's Flying Circus.

questions.prompt: Who proposed a famous test for whether a machine can think, and is called the father of computer science?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing proposed the "imitation game", now called the Turing test, in 1950.

questions.prompt: Which scanner uses a strong magnet and radio waves, not X-rays, to image the body?
questions.explanation: MRI = magnetic resonance imaging. CT uses X-rays; ultrasound uses sound waves.

questions.prompt: What does "GPT" stand for in ChatGPT?
questions.explanation: Transformer is the neural-network design behind most modern AI language models.

questions.prompt: The first successful human heart transplant was done in 1967 in which country?
questions.explanation: Dr Christiaan Barnard performed it in Cape Town, South Africa.

questions.prompt: Nepal's flag is the only national flag in the world that isn't a rectangle.
questions.explanation: Its two stacked pennants make it unique among national flags.

questions.prompt: What is the national flower of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Lali Gurans (rhododendron) turns the hills red every spring.

questions.prompt: Where was Gautama Buddha born?
questions.explanation: Lumbini, in Nepal, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.prompt: What is the national bird of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Danphe (Himalayan monal) is famous for its shimmering rainbow feathers.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers about a third of Earth's surface, more than all the land combined.

questions.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: It hangs in the Louvre in Paris, behind bulletproof glass.

questions.prompt: Which is the longest river in Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Karnali starts in Tibet and runs through western Nepal.

questions.prompt: Who reached the top of Mount Everest with Tenzing Norgay Sherpa in 1953?
questions.explanation: They reached the summit on 29 May 1953.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City is only about 0.44 km², smaller than many college campuses!

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.prompt: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.explanation: Mandarin has the most native speakers; English has the most speakers overall.

questions.prompt: What is the largest desert in the world?
questions.explanation: A desert is defined by low rainfall, not heat. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

questions.prompt: What is the official height of Mount Everest, as measured in 2020?
questions.explanation: Measured jointly by Nepal and China. 8,611 m is K2, and 8,586 m is Kangchenjunga.

questions.prompt: In which year was the current Constitution of Nepal promulgated?
questions.explanation: It was promulgated on 20 September 2015 (Asoj 3, 2072 BS).

questions.prompt: Which country has the most time zones?
questions.explanation: France has 12, thanks to overseas territories around the world. Russia has 11.

questions.prompt: Who is the current Prime Minister of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Balen Shah was sworn in on 27 March 2026, becoming Nepal's youngest Prime Minister.

questions.prompt: Before politics, Nepal's Prime Minister Balen Shah was known as a rapper.
questions.explanation: He was a rapper, then Mayor of Kathmandu (2022–2026), before becoming Prime Minister.

questions.prompt: Which country won the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: Spain beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time on 19 July 2026, their second title after 2010.

questions.prompt: Which team won the 2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup?
questions.explanation: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs in Ahmedabad on 8 March 2026, becoming the first team to win three T20 World Cups.

questions.prompt: The 2026 Asian Games opened on 19 September. Which country is hosting them?
questions.explanation: Aichi and Nagoya, Japan, host the Games from 19 September to 4 October 2026.

questions.prompt: Who became Nepal's first female Prime Minister in September 2025?
questions.explanation: Sushila Karki, also Nepal's first female Chief Justice, led the interim government after the Gen Z protests.

questions.prompt: Which party won a majority in Nepal's March 2026 general election?
questions.explanation: The RSP won 182 of the 275 seats in the House of Representatives.

questions.prompt: Nepal won a match at the 2026 T20 World Cup.
questions.explanation: Nepal beat Scotland by 7 wickets at Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium, their first T20 World Cup win since 2014.

questions.prompt: Which country topped the medal table at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan–Cortina?
questions.explanation: Norway won a record 18 gold medals, the most by any country at a single Winter Games.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, NASA's Artemis II flew astronauts around the Moon: the first crewed Moon mission since which program?
questions.explanation: The last crewed Moon mission was Apollo 17 in 1972.

questions.prompt: Besides the USA, which country had an astronaut on the Artemis II crew?
questions.explanation: Canada's Jeremy Hansen flew with NASA's Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch.

questions.prompt: Who is the current Pope, elected in May 2025?
questions.explanation: Pope Leo XIV is the first Pope from the United States.

questions.prompt: Name this landmark.
questions.explanation: One of the largest stupas in the world, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.prompt: This heritage site isn't far from NIET. What is it?
questions.explanation: Patan (Lalitpur) Durbar Square, full of Newar architecture, just south of Kupondole.

questions.prompt: Who is this famous scientist?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein: relativity, E = mc², and the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.

questions.explanation: "I'm the king of the world!" (1997)

questions.explanation: Hakuna Matata!

questions.explanation: Lub-dub: the sound of heart valves closing, heard through a stethoscope. Biomedical engineers design those!

questions.prompt: We've zoomed right in. Which famous landmark is this?
questions.explanation: Paris, 1889: once the tallest structure in the world.

questions.prompt: Who is this scientist?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie, the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two sciences (Physics and Chemistry).

questions.prompt: Name this electronic component.
questions.explanation: A resistor. Its coloured bands tell you its resistance value.

questions.prompt: Which country's flag is this?
questions.explanation: Bhutan: the dragon (Druk) holds jewels for wealth and protection.

questions.prompt: Which animal makes this sound?
questions.explanation: Dolphins use clicks and whistles to find their way (echolocation).

questions.prompt: Which traditional Nepali instrument is this?
questions.explanation: The Sarangi, a bowed string instrument carved from a single piece of wood, traditionally played by the Gandarbha community.

questions.prompt: What is this desk toy called?
questions.explanation: Newton's cradle shows conservation of momentum and energy.

questions.prompt: Before Wi-Fi… what made this sound?
questions.explanation: A dial-up modem connecting to the internet over a phone line. Ask your parents!

questions.prompt: This is seen under a microscope. What is it?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells: disc-shaped with a dip in the middle, and no nucleus.
